one_liner: Senior USPHS Commissioned Corps nurse/clinician billet leading ICE Health Service Corps medical escort missions by air, land, and sea, supervising flight nurses.
fit_summary: Only current USPHS commissioned officers can apply, and it requires an RN, PA-C or NP license, more than six years of acute care and prior special operations unit management. Daniel has none of these, so he cannot qualify.
eligibility: Open only to current USPHS Commissioned Corps officers; Call to Active Duty candidates are excluded. The 'public' hiring-path tag on USAJOBS is misleading.
Must be a clinical professional (RN, PA-C, or NP) with more than 6 years in ER, ICU, or another acute care setting.
Requires at least 2 years as ISOU program manager or 1 year as ISOU SC, plus at least 2 years of supervisory experience.
Must attain and maintain a DHS Secret clearance, an official passport, ICE credentials, CPR/BLS/ACLS, and pass an FAA Class III flight physical and a swim test.
keywords: represents to other Federal and non-Federal agencies
strategy: Do not apply to this posting. You are not a USPHS officer or licensed clinician, and HR will screen you out at the eligibility step.

Use this posting's language to find civilian DHS roles that fit you, such as FEMA emergency management specialist (GS-0089), program analyst (GS-0343), or intergovernmental affairs positions open to the public.

Frame your IEM work around government clients served, the disaster recovery or preparedness programs you supported, and any stakeholder coordination you did, using the terms 'Federal, State and local' and 'interagency coordination.'
Keep your federal resume to two pages and list dates, hours per week, and a brief statement of specialized experience for each job.

Save a USAJOBS search for FEMA and DHS jobs open to 'U.S. citizens' within commuting distance of Manassas or with remote options. Also check Virginia VDEM and the Prince William County and Fairfax County emergency management offices.
interview_questions: Describe a time you coordinated among multiple government agencies under time pressure.
How have you evaluated a program's effectiveness and reported metrics to leadership?
Tell us about delivering difficult information to a public or stakeholder audience.
How do you adapt when mission priorities change suddenly?
watch_outs: Eligibility is limited to current USPHS commissioned officers, so this posting is closed to Daniel.
It requires a clinical license, acute care experience and unit-specific experience his resume doesn't show.
